title: The Ramgharia Grievance Closes as Dileram's Wealth Appears

blocks.text: This page first completes the brief grievance against the Ramgharia-related offenders by recalling how their revenues spread across several regions and how shocking their conduct had become. They had the audacity to capture Jassa Singh Ahluwalia, and the narrative treats that act as bringing judgment on their line.

Having closed that moral reckoning, the poem opens a wider Lahore-centered story around Dileram. He is introduced as a man of rank, enormous stored wealth, and political importance in a period unsettled by Abdali, Maratha movement, and pressure on the Lahore nawab.

The page therefore works as another hinge. One episode ends in judgment on past insult, while the next begins by following where wealth is hidden, transferred, and protected when larger powers destabilize the region.
